step1_analysis.description: This circuit is the active core of a cascode low-noise amplifier with a source follower output buffer. XM1 is the main amplifying common-source transistor (with source degeneration), XM2 is the cascode transistor to reduce the Miller effect and improve isolation, and XM3 is a source follower acting as an output buffer to drive the subsequent stages.

paper_reference.title: An Ultrawideband CMOS Low-Noise Amplifier for 3.1–10.6-GHz Wireless Receivers

power_consumption.description: Total DC power consumed by the amplifier core and buffer.

sky130_expected.calculation: P = VDD * I_total. Assuming a bias current of ~5mA from a 1.8V supply to match the paper's power target.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Adjusted bias voltages and transistor sizing in the testbench to target ~9mW total power consumption on SKY130's 1.8V supply.

voltage_gain.description: Mid-band AC voltage gain of the amplifier.

sky130_expected.calculation: Gain ≈ gm1 * R_load. With gm1 ≈ 20mS and R_load = 300Ω, intrinsic gain is ~15 dB. The source follower attenuates this slightly.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Expected to be around 10 dB to match the paper, heavily dependent on the chosen load resistor/inductor in the testbench.

bandwidth.description: Operating frequency range where gain is within 3dB of its maximum.

sky130_expected.calculation: Determined by the RC time constant at the cascode output node (V_OUT). f_3dB ≈ 1 / (2 * π * R_load * C_parasitic).
sky130_expected.reasoning: Without the paper's input Chebyshev filter and inductive peaking, the bare circuit acts as a low-pass amplifier. The unity-gain frequency will extend into the multi-GHz range.

noise_figure.description: Signal-to-noise ratio degradation caused by the amplifier.

sky130_expected.calculation: Dominated by the input transistor XM1. NF ≈ 10 * log10(1 + γ * gdo / gm1).
sky130_expected.reasoning: SKY130 0.15µm devices have comparable noise performance to 0.18µm devices, so ~4 dB is expected.

iip3.description: Input third-order intercept point, measuring linearity.

sky130_expected.calculation: Proportional to the overdrive voltage (Vgs - Vth) of XM1.
sky130_expected.reasoning: A higher overdrive voltage improves linearity at the cost of power consumption.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure DC power consumption, AC voltage gain, and unity-gain bandwidth of the UWB LNA core. Passives and biasing are added to make the bare transistors function as an amplifier.
step3_testbench.spice:
* UWB LNA Testbench
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

* Parameterized sizing for RF performance (~5mA total current)
.param W_xm1=50u L_xm1=0.15u
.param W_xm2=50u L_xm2=0.15u
.param W_xm3=20u L_xm3=0.15u

* DUT (Extracted from paper)
XM2 V_OUT V_CAS N4 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm2} w={W_xm2}
XM3 VDD V_OUT V_OUT_PRIME GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm3} w={W_xm3}
XM1 N4 N8 N3 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}

* Biasing and Passives
VVDD VDD 0 1.8
V_CAS V_CAS 0 1.2
V_BIAS N8_bias 0 0.7
R_bias N8_bias N8 10k
C_in IN N8 10p
V_IN IN 0 dc 0 ac 1
L_deg N3 0 0.5n
R_load VDD V_OUT 300
R_out V_OUT_PRIME 0 500

.control
* 1. DC Operating Point for Power Consumption
op
let power = -i(VVDD) * 1.8
print power

* 2. AC Analysis for Gain and Bandwidth
ac dec 50 100Meg 100G
let gain_db = vdb(V_OUT_PRIME)

* Measure mid-band gain at 1 GHz
meas ac gain_1G find gain_db at=1G

* Measure unity gain frequency (0 dB crossing)
meas ac f_unity when gain_db=0 fall=1

quit
.endc
.end
